newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court to publish pay ruling, govt to appeal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court to publish pay ruling, govt to appeal.

text.p: Brazil's highest court was due Friday to formally publish its February verdict to give a 28.9 percent pay rise to 11 federal workers, paving the way for the government to appeal the controverial ruling, an official said.
The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) ruled in February in favor of 11 federal workers who claimed they were entitled to a 28.9 percent increases given to the armed forces in 1993.
Since then hundreds of thousands of other federal workers and pensioners have begun legal proceedings for similar rises, threatening to add billions of dollars onto the government's payroll.
In one case currently in a court in Rio, about 120,000 people are demanding the 29.8 percent rise.

An official with the Federal Advocacy, the government's lawyers, said officials would study the official version of the STF's ruling before lodging an appeal. The government has ten days from Friday to appeal.

Finance Ministry officials have argued that pay increases and bonuses awarded the 11 workers between 1993 and February this year mean they have in fact already received some of the 28.9 percent increase which therefore should be reduced.
Analysts say the case could represent a threat to Brazil's attempts to rein in public spending, but not in the short term.

"This is not a problem for 1997 nor 1998," said Mauro Schneider, an analyst with ING Barings. He said the government would only give workers the pay rise once their cases had gone through the entire legal system, culminating in the STF.
